title: First Experimental Results of Space Object Detection Using the InteRFeX Array

problem.summary: This paper presents the first experimental validation of InteRFeX, a non-uniform receive only (passive) array located at the Nova Systems Space Precinct in Peterborough, Australia, designed for space domain awareness applications.
statements: This paper presents the first experimental validation of InteRFeX, a non-uniform receive only (passive) array located at the Nova Systems Space Precinct in Peterborough, Australia, designed for space domain awareness applications.

It operates over a frequency range of 70 to 300 MHz and is capable of functioning in a range of observational modes, including as a coherent passive bistatic radar for space surveillance, which is the focus of this work.

InteRFeX exploits commercial broadcast transmissions as illuminators of opportunity, combining crossambiguity function processing for bistatic range and range-rate retrieval with MUSIC-based direction-of-arrival (DoA) estimation for angular localization.

components: It is a dedicated SDA instrument with the intention of enabling continuous data capture and monitoring of the Space Domain.

InteRFeX has an operational frequency range of 70-300 MHz, and can observe in multiple operating modes, including as a radio interferometer, and, as described in this paper, as a passive bistatic radar receiver.
The array consists of 16 elements, called Tiles, situated in a randomly perturbed grid over a total area of approximately 35 m × 35 m.
